evidence.quote: Several specific open problems that exist in this context are mentioned in~\cite[Section~9]{NieStr24}. More generally, try to extend the approach in~\cite{GerMadNieStr19,GerNieStr20,GerNieStr22,NieStr24} to other types of PDEs or preconditioners.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a partial differential equation (PDE) discretized by a standard numerical method (e.g., finite differences, finite elements, isogeometric analysis) on a sequence of grids of increasing resolution, producing a sequence of large sparse matrices $\{A_n\}$ whose dimensions $d_n \to \infty$. Assume $A_n$ is paired with a preconditioner $P_n$ so that one studies the spectrum of $P_n^{-1} A_n$. A spectral symbol for the sequence $\{P_n^{-1} A_n\}$ is a measurable function $f : \Omega \to \mathbb{C}$ (with $\Omega$ a domain of finite measure) such that, for every continuous compactly supported test function $F$,
$$\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{d_n} \sum_{j=1}^{d_n} F(\lambda_j(P_n^{-1} A_n)) = \frac{1}{|\Omega|} \int_{\Omega} F(f(x))\, dx.$$
Suppose that for a particular family of PDEs (e.g., constant-coefficient elliptic problems on tensor-product domains) and a particular family of preconditioners (e.g., multigrid, ILU, or Schwarz-type), one has identified explicit spectral symbols $f$ that fully describe the asymptotic eigenvalue distribution of $\{P_n^{-1} A_n\}$, including localization of outlier eigenvalues and conditioning estimates.

Problem: Extend this symbol-based spectral analysis to broader classes of PDEs and/or preconditioners. Specifically, identify and rigorously prove explicit spectral symbols $f$ describing the asymptotic eigenvalue distribution of $\{P_n^{-1} A_n\}$ in settings such as: (i) variable-coefficient or non-self-adjoint elliptic operators; (ii) time-dependent (parabolic or hyperbolic) PDEs and their all-at-once or space-time discretizations; (iii) saddle-point or coupled multi-physics systems (e.g., Stokes, Maxwell); and (iv) preconditioners not previously covered by such an analysis, including algebraic multigrid, domain decomposition with inexact subdomain solves, and sparse approximate inverse preconditioners. In each case, determine whether the resulting symbol yields uniform spectral clustering away from zero and dimension-independent convergence rates for standard Krylov iterations.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as a general research direction: extending symbol-based (GLT-style) spectral analysis of preconditioned PDE matrices to additional PDE classes and preconditioners. Such extensions are an active area of research with many specific subproblems remaining open; no single comprehensive resolution is known.

status_evidence.title: Generalized Locally Toeplitz Sequences: Theory and Applications
status_evidence.snippet: Monograph series describing GLT theory and listing ongoing extensions to new PDE discretizations and preconditioners.
status_evidence.claim: Extending symbol-based spectral analysis to further PDEs/preconditioners is an ongoing program with open subproblems.
